review_notes: I read the whole file and its test file (AdicModulesTest/CompletedIntegers.lean). I also read downstream uses of the ring equivalence lemma in CompletedLocalStructure, CompletedValuationComposite and PrincipalAdicSpectrum. I checked Mathlib for existing simp coverage of the subring `algebraMap`, of `UniformSpace.Completion.algebraMap_def`, and of `AlgEquiv.commutes`. The two simp lemmas `algebraMap_completionIntegers_apply` and `coe_algebraMap_completionIntegers` look fine. Mathlib's `algebraMap_ofSubsemiring_apply` is not simp, and `UniformSpace.Completion.algebraMap_def` is not simp, so neither is covered or competed with. I found no loop or competing rule. The one finding is a minor redundancy and inconsistency in the simp interface for the comparison equivalence. I did not run Lean, so I did not check how simp behaves on these terms.

findings.problem: The simp interface for the comparison is split inconsistently. The public comparison is the `AlgEquiv` `principalAdicCompletionEquiv`. Its algebra-map identity is a plain, non-simp lemma, while the same identity for the auxiliary `RingEquiv` carries `@[simp]`. Mathlib's simp lemma `AlgEquiv.commutes` already rewrites `principalAdicCompletionEquiv a ha0 (algebraMap V _ x)` to `algebraMap V _ x`, because the equivalence is built with `commutes'`. The test file's `canonicalMapClient` proves exactly this statement with `simp`. So the non-simp lemma duplicates an existing simp rule and adds no new rewrite. Its only use in this file is `rw` inside `principalAdicCompletionEquiv_symm_eq_algebraMap_iff`. The `@[simp]` rule is the one that does not need to be public: it fires only on the auxiliary `RingEquiv`, which users of the `AlgEquiv` API do not meet. Downstream files name that lemma explicitly, for example `simpa [A, principalAdicCompletionRingEquiv_algebraMap]`, so it is not the canonical rule for the public equivalence.
findings.proposed_change: Either delete `principalAdicCompletionEquiv_algebraMap` and rely on `AlgEquiv.commutes`, replacing its single `rw` use with `AlgEquiv.commutes _ x`, or keep it and document that it is a named restatement of `AlgEquiv.commutes`. Keep `@[simp]` on `principalAdicCompletionRingEquiv_algebraMap`, since it is needed for the ring equivalence. Do not add a simp lemma that rewrites `principalAdicCompletionEquiv` to the ring equivalence. That would push the public `AlgEquiv` toward the auxiliary one and could interfere with `AlgEquiv.symm` and `commutes` lemmas.
findings.benefit: There is a single canonical simp route for each of the two equivalences, with no duplicate identity for readers to keep in sync. Users of the `AlgEquiv` get the simplification from the standard Mathlib lemma, and the `@[simp]` set contains no unused near-duplicate.
